bull.b: Repeated bookings growth indicates durable user demand and expanding marketplace activity. Cross-platform adoption, enterprise mobility and record first-time users can support continued penetration across Uber’s large global network.

High and closely aligned free cash flow supports earnings quality and gives Uber internal funding for technology, partnerships, acquisitions and shareholder returns. This reduces dependence on external capital as the platform scales.

Lower leverage and a substantially larger equity base improve financial resilience and flexibility. A stronger balance sheet gives Uber more capacity to invest in growth initiatives while absorbing operating volatility across markets.

bear.b: The gap between bookings and reported revenue growth shows that monetization is not keeping pace with activity. Although much of the decline reflects a U.K. business-model change, sustained investment and competition could limit margin expansion.

Autonomous vehicles could strengthen Uber’s long-term supply economics, but commercialization remains very early relative to the planned capital commitment. Deployment, utilization and partner execution must improve before returns can offset the investment burden.

bear.t: Delivery Hero Integration and Financing Risk
bear.b: The acquisition could broaden Uber’s combined mobility and delivery footprint, but its scale raises integration, competition-clearance and financing risks. Execution missteps or slower synergies could pressure leverage, management focus and returns.
